lessons.title: What CTI names
lessons.why: The name is older than any of the products in this track. The vendor page still has to say what the product actually does.
depends: a telephone system you can name
body: Wikipedia’s page for computer telephony integration says computer-telephony integration, also called computer–telephone integration or CTI, is a general term for technologies that coordinate interactions between telephones and computers. The following sentence on that page is marked citation needed. This room stops at the sourced sentence.

Dynamics 365 and Salesforce each publish a specific bridge. CTI is the family name. It is not a configuration screen, and it does not tell you whether the representative answers in Teams, in a CRM workspace, or in a partner desktop.

chart.title: Name, then product
chart.note: Teaching order. Not a count of products.

lessons.say: CTI names the coordination. The vendor page names the product.
lessons.fault: A design says CTI and never says which app answers the call.
lessons.listen: CTI is the general name for coordinating a telephone and a computer. Open the vendor page before you configure anything.

lessons.title: The Dynamics voice channel
lessons.why: The voice channel is the Dynamics page that says where PSTN calling lives, and which app the representative uses.
depends: Dynamics 365 Contact Center or Customer Service
body: The introduction to the voice channel applies to Dynamics 365 Contact Center embedded, Dynamics 365 Contact Center standalone, and Dynamics 365 Customer Service. It says representatives receive and make PSTN calls through a native calling experience in Dynamics 365, and that the voice channel is built on Azure Communication Services. The same page says routing a voice call uses unified routing, the same way an incoming chat is assigned, and that a Copilot Studio agent can be the conversational IVR because it shares the platform.

The capabilities table on that page includes call controls, music on hold and on wait, customer and case lookup, emergency dialing currently supported in the United States and Puerto Rico only, a callback number, distribution of incoming calls, voicemail, outbound calls, transfer to an external number, phone-number provisioning, skills-based assignment, transcription, recording, sentiment, translation, supervisor monitor and barge, a post-call survey, and queue-position announcements. This room does not copy the marketing sections above that table.

lessons.title: Teams Phone into the voice channel
lessons.why: A Teams number can be the PSTN path. The page that allows it also limits which Calling Plan numbers qualify.
depends: Teams Phone connectivity you can name
body: The page Configure Teams Phone in the voice channel says the PSTN connectivity is a Teams Calling Plan, Operator Connect, or Direct Routing. For a Teams Calling Plan, that page says service numbers only are supported. It also lists Enterprise Voice, outbound-calling prerequisites, and a licensing guide. This room does not copy SKU names from the licensing guide.

Synchronization needs the Teams Administrator or Teams Telephony Administrator role, and the delegated Graph permission TeamsResourceAccount.Read.All with admin consent. The page says a Teams resource account is required for every number used with Dynamics 365 Contact Center. Direct Routing uses Set-CsPhoneNumberAssignment with PhoneNumberType DirectRouting, then Grant-CsOnlineVoiceRoutingPolicy. Operator Connect uses PhoneNumberType OperatorConnect.

lessons.title: The resource account and the number
lessons.why: The number does not appear in Dynamics until the resource account exists and someone runs Sync from Teams.
body: The same page shows Connect-MicrosoftTeams, then New-CsOnlineApplicationInstance, then Set-CsOnlineApplicationInstance and Sync-CsOnlineApplicationInstance. Those last two examples include an ApplicationId and the organization’s Azure Communication Services resource ID. Copy both from the current page. This room does not ask you to memorize the identifier.

After the license and the service number are on the resource account, the page says to open Copilot Service admin center, Channels, Phone numbers, Advanced, the Teams phone system tab, and Sync from Teams. Then create a workstream and add a voice channel for that number. When a customer calls, the representative receives the notification in the Copilot Service workspace app. If recording is enabled, an announcement plays. If an outbound conversation is not created, the page says the representative gets an alert and should initiate the call again.

lessons.fault: The number is assigned in Teams and never synced, so Dynamics has no voice channel for it.

lessons.title: Salesforce Voice and Partner Contact Center
lessons.why: The old name is still in product screens. The pages opened for this room say what the current name is.
depends: the two pages named in the sources
body: The help page opened for this room is titled Connect Voice from a Partner Contact Center. It says Salesforce Voice with Telephony Providers, formerly Service Cloud Voice, is now part of Partner Contact Center, and that you may still see the older name. Its learning map lists the Telephony Integration REST API, the Voice Toolkit API, and Lambda functions for Amazon Connect under Develop.

The same note still names Salesforce Voice with Amazon Connect, Salesforce Voice with Partner Telephony, and Salesforce Voice with Partner Telephony from Amazon Connect. It points to Agentforce Contact Center Voice for a built-in telephony offering. This room does not describe that offering beyond the pointer. A Salesforce developer-guide URL was requested during this build and did not open, so this room does not quote it.
lessons.say: Service Cloud Voice is now Salesforce Voice, and the help page places it in Partner Contact Center.
lessons.fault: A design uses only the old name and misses which telephony model the page still lists.
lessons.listen: Salesforce’s guide says Service Cloud Voice is now Salesforce Voice. The help page says that voice offering is now part of Partner Contact Center.

lessons.why: The help page does not collapse the telephony models into one setup path.

body: The learning map on Connect Voice from a Partner Contact Center lists separate setup paths: Partner Contact Center with Amazon Connect, Partner Contact Center Voice, and Partner Contact Center with Amazon Connect as bring your own. It also lists supervisor listen-in and barge-in, linking calls with customer contact records, and the Telephony Integration REST API and Voice Toolkit API under Develop.

This room does not add editions, government-cloud limits, or prices. Those were not on the help page that opened. The developer-guide URL did not open from this build, so it is marked confirm and it is not quoted.

lessons.title: The call-to-record seam
lessons.why: The bridge fails when the call and the CRM record do not share an identifier you stored.
depends: the two CRM bridges in this track
body: Microsoft’s Teams contact-center article describes three provider models. Extend uses the Teams client as the calling endpoint. The Dynamics Teams Phone page, which is a different article, says the representative receives the Teams-number call in the Copilot Service workspace app. Those are different desktops. Do not describe the Dynamics workspace as the Extend client.

The Salesforce learning map includes Link Calls with Customer Contact Records. Store the number and the call identifier the product gives you, and test a record that should not match. The Dynamics voice-channel table includes customer and case lookup. A lookup that returns the wrong record is a data fault, not a codec fault. Track 17’s CRM room is the place for the screen-pop fields this campus already names.
